title: A Uniform for the Harbor
premise: In 1848, in a Baltic port city on the edge of uprising, Oscar Eriksen has spent her life passing as her father's son so she can inherit his typeface-cutting trade. When a stranger arrives with letters written in the unmistakable hand of her brother Anders—declared dead at sea three years ago—Oscar learns he survived, joined the revolutionaries, and needs one berth on the last ship out before the harbor closes. The stranger's price is the Eriksens' printing press, and her father, drunk on the power the revolution offers common men, would rather burn the shop than bargain. In the end, Oscar forges her father's name to sell the press, gives the berth to Anders, stays behind herself to face the authorities—and discovers that the identity she fought to hide was the only self worth keeping.
about_author: Zephyrine Zhou is a former letterpress compositor who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century print equipment in coastal museum archives across Northern Europe. Her fiction draws on the ledgers, broadsides, and marginalia she catalogued, giving voice to the invisible hands behind historical upheavals.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Letters
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. She cuts type by lamplight while her father drinks downstairs, establishing the shop, the disguise she maintains as 'his son,' and her belief that revolutions happen elsewhere. Emotional beat: quiet resignation mistaken for contentment.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Composing Stick
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A rain-soaked stranger named Voss arrives asking for the Eriksen press, carrying letters in Anders's handwriting. Oscar recognizes it instantly but says nothing. Beat: the floor tilts; invisibility ends.

chapters.title: Dead Men Write Neatly
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. He explains Anders survived a shipwreck, fell in with radicals, and needs passage out before the naval blockade. He offers coin for use of the press to print pamphlets. Beat: temptation wrapped in grief.

chapters.title: Father of the New Age
chapters.summary: Father Eriksen's POV. He meets Voss and is electrified—the revolution promises men like him power. He agrees to print, not for Anders, but for glory. Beat: first taste of corruption.

chapters.title: What the Sister Cut
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Flashback to how the disguise began: her mother's death, her father's grief, the practical lie that hardened into law. Beat: tenderness curdling into resentment.

chapters.title: Pamphlets by Morning
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The family prints seditious broadsides overnight; Oscar sets the type beautifully, unable to stop her craft serving a cause she distrusts. Beat: complicity.

chapters.title: The Harbor Closes Its Hand
chapters.summary: Harbormaster Lindqvist's POV. The navy announces the port seals at week's end; one civilian vessel may sail on the morning tide. Lists are drawn. Beat: the clock starts.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Berth
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Voss reveals there is only one berth and Anders expects it for himself—or for Oscar, if she'll come. Father assumes it is his due as the movement's printer. Beat: dread arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Committee of the Faithful
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Local radicals meet in the cellar; Father grandstands, promising the press to the cause. Voss privately warns Oscar that power is already remaking her father. Beat: warning unheeded.

chapters.title: Ink Under the Fingernails
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A raid scare forces them to hide the press; Oscar and Voss work close through the night and an unspoken understanding forms. Beat: warmth amid danger.

chapters.title: My Brother's Ghost Argues Politics
chapters.summary: Anders's POV, via a smuggled letter read aloud. He writes of ideals, of guilt over leaving, of asking Oscar—not Father—to decide the berth. Beat: the choice lands squarely on her.

chapters.title: The Red Broadside
chapters.summary: Father's POV. His pamphlet incites a riot at the customs house; three men die. He feels exalted, then briefly horrified, then exalted again. Beat: corruption takes root.

chapters.title: Lindqvist Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The harbormaster, an old customer, hints he knows what they print and offers to look away—for the berth, or for her silence about his own dealings. Beat: everyone is bargaining with something rotten.

chapters.title: Which Child Was I
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Confronting her father, she nearly confesses she is his daughter; he interrupts, praising 'his son' as heir, and she swallows the truth again. Beat: heartbreak of the unsaid.

chapters.title: The Press Must Burn
chapters.summary: Father's POV. Authorities close in; Father decides to torch the shop as martyrdom, taking the evidence and the family's livelihood with it. Beat: power fully corrupted into destruction.

chapters.title: Night of the Firebrands
chapters.summary: Alternating Oscar/Voss. They discover Father's plan hours before dawn; Voss urges escape, Oscar refuses to let the press—or the truth—burn. Beat: rising panic toward climax.

chapters.title: The Forger's Daughter
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, climax begins. Using her mastery of type and hand, Oscar forges her father's signature on papers selling the press to Voss's network, legally moving it before the fire can be set. Beat: her hidden skill becomes salvation.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Tide Line
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, climax. On the quay at dawn, Father discovers the sale and the forgery; in the struggle of wills, Oscar finally declares who she is. Beat: the mask comes off publicly.

chapters.title: One Berth, Given
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Anders arrives disguised among stevedores; Oscar puts him on the ship instead of herself, choosing to stay and answer for the pamphlets under her own true name. Beat: sacrifice as self-claiming.

chapters.title: What the Ash Kept
chapters.summary: Father's POV. The fire he set consumes the empty shop; arrested, he sees his children clearly for the first time—one gone, one standing unbowed. Beat: ruin as terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Setting Type in a New Season
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Months later, acquitted through Lindqvist's testimony, she works at the relocated press under her own name, printing fair accounts rather than slogans. Beat: quiet rebuilding.

chapters.title: A Uniform for the Harbor
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, coda. A letter from Anders arrives; she reads it aloud to the apprentices, including girls she now trains openly. History, she understands, happened to her all along. Beat: memory claimed, identity whole.
